label: text
content: BEFORE I proceed to my Second Letter, I think it proper to remove an Objection which has been made to my First.

label: text
content: I allow'd, that if the Sacrament was a mere humane Institution, that if Jesus as a Man, and independently of God, instituted it, that then the End for which it was instituted, would very probably be the Remembrance of himself. And consequently that whoever seriously and religiously remember'd him in the Actions of eating Bread and drinking Wine, would perform those Actions suitably to the End of the Institution, and acceptably to the Institutor. And that in this Case, the Institutor could not require antecedent moral Dispositions or Behaviour as Qualifications in those Persons who should comply with

label: text

label: text
content: And further, it is the revealed Will of God, that God only is to be worshipped with Religious Worship.

label: text
content: Consequently, if any Man should assume to himself Divine Honours, it is our Duty to disobey him.

label: text
content: This is both the Doctrine of Reason and Scripture.

content: But the Sacrament is an Institution where Religious Worship is render'd to Jesus Christ; consequently if it was a mere human Institution we could not comply with it acceptably to God. And if Man assumes to himself that Worship which belongs to God; or if he insti-

content: AND what reason we have to believe that these Declarations extend to all his Positive Institutions.

label: text
content: WHETHER those Declarations which were given to guard God's Ordinances from the Approaches of the Wicked under the Jewish Dispensation, are not guards also to this great Christian Ordinance.

label: text
content: AND whether if the New Testament were altogether silent, with regard to the terms of a Christian's acceptance with God, in this great Christian Ordinance, an Interpreter of the will of God ought not from the Old Testament to pronounce, that wilful Habitual Sinners at the Time they are such, have nothing to do to take this Covenant of God in their Mouths.

label: text
content: But 2dly. Be pleased, Sir, to search the New Testament itself, and you will, I am confident, find, that in this weighty point, it is not without many Witnesses.

label: text
content: BE pleased to Examine the Tenor and Scope of the New Testament, as well as those particular Texts, which immediately relate to this Duty.

label: text
content: BE pleased again to Examine your Interpretation of the 1 Cor. V. and fee whe-

label: text
content: ther the Feast which the Apostle speaks of, can be the perpetual Feast, which a Society of Christians are keeping, as it were, under the Sense of their deliverance, and of the Love of their Deliverer.

label: text
content: Be pleased to consider, whether if St Paul designed to exclude open notorious Sinners from the Lord's Supper, these Sinners could partake of this Supper acceptably to Gqd.

label: text
content: BE pleased again to consider that remarkable Passage to the Corinthians, and see whether the Apostle, when he said, But let a Man Examine himself, and so let him eat &c. could really bid these Corinthians enter into, and try themselves by considering the Original Institution of this Holy Rite; or, as you afterwards put it, Examine their own Hearts and Dispositions by the Institution of this Holy Rite, in order to assure themselves that they come to the Lord's Supper, and will behave themselves at it, not as a Common Meal; &c. I am not now pleading for my own Interpretations: but what I ask of you, is that you would again consider, whether yours can be the Senfe of St. Paul.

label: text
content: AND if you should find that you have mistaken Scripture in any one instance, this will I am perfwaded lead you to make

label: text
content: a thorough search into the Evidence of your Doctrine.

label: text
content: You say, It would be in me * a fineful presumption to amuse Christians with greater and higher expectations, than they, who alone can be depended on, as far as I can judge, have given any reason to entertain.

label: text
content: VERY true : but I apprehend it would be no less an inexcusable presumption to amuse wilful habitual Sinners, with greater, and higher expectations, than they who alone can be depended on, have given them any reason to entertain.

label: text
content: This would be sowing pillows to Armholes +; crying, Peace+, Peace, when there is, No Peace. A mistake here is of dangerous consequence.

label: text
content: AND when, Sir, you are comparing your Doctrine with the Holy Scripture, be pleased to examine your Paraphrase upon the words of our Saviour; and see whether you have really observed your own Rule, and put no meaning upon the words of Christ, but what is agreeable to the common Rules of speaking in the like Caeses ||.

label: text
content: I THINK, I may say, that Paraphrase cannot be the Sense of the words of our Saviour.

label: text
content: As to the Liturgy of the Church of England, when it has been objected that you have not given the Sense of the Comp. of it, it has been answered, But you have given a better, you have made the Duty rational one. Very well: we will at present take this Answer with regard to the Liturgy: but this will not do for Scripture. To mend Scripture, is to destroy it. And if Scripture is gone, then where is the Duty it self?

label: text
content: As then, Sir, you would avoid the terrible Imputation of putting Interpretations upon Scripture, not agreeable to the common Rules of speaking in the like Cafes; (which you have been by multitudes of People accused of) you are desired, either to give some new Light and Evidence to your Interpretations, or give up that Doctrine which you say you have drawn from the New Testament.

label: text
content: IF you forbear to do one of these, we of the Laity must change the Question, and desire you to inform us, upon what foot receiving the Sacrament duty.
